official.application_cycle: Cohort 4 of Phase II (Phase II commenced October 2025, three cohorts)
official.status_note: The official call ran 20 August to 10 September 2026, 17:00 EAT, and that window has closed; the page timeline continues with communication of successful students and host universities in December 2026, and acceptance of offers and signing of scholarship agreements in December 2026
official.tuition_coverage_note: Full tuition fees payable directly to the host university
benefits: Full tuition fees payable directly to the host university
Monthly stipend of EUR 380 to cover accommodation, meals, local transport and other living expenses
One return economy-class air ticket between the scholar's home country and the host country upon commencement and completion of studies
EUR 200 arrival allowance upon arrival in the study country and opening a bank account
Lump-sum allowance of EUR 650 for study materials and a one-time EUR 1,500 study and research allowance
Medical insurance for the duration of the scholarship, plus visa/entry fee where an entry pass or student pass is required, and participation in at least one extracurricular event
eligibility: Citizen of any of the 8 EAC Partner States: Burundi, Democratic Republic of Congo, Kenya, Rwanda, Somalia, South Sudan, United Republic of Tanzania and Uganda
Below 35 years of age at the time of application
Apply to study in an EAC Partner State other than the country of citizenship
Bachelor's Degree with a minimum of Second Class Upper Division, Distinction or equivalent qualification
Have applied for admission to an eligible Master's programme offered by a partner university
Submit a complete scholarship application within the stipulated application period
requirements: Apply for admission to a partner university in an EAC Partner State other than the country of citizenship, indicating intention to apply for the EAC Scholarship Programme and paying the university application fee where applicable
Complete and submit the separate online EAC Scholarship Application form
Submit all supporting documents in a single zipped PDF folder, with files named by the prescribed document codes
Email the zipped folder to eacsp@iucea.org and scholarships@adroitconsultinternational.com with the prescribed subject line format

Submit the application in English; foreign qualifications must be equated by the host country's competent authority before admission, and non-English transcripts and certificates translated by an accredited provider
documents: E02 Passport photograph in colour of full head and upper shoulders
E03 Proof of university admission application (admission letter, acknowledgement email, receipt or portal screenshot)
E04 Certified true copies of Bachelor's degree certificate and academic transcript
E06 Bank statements for the last six months, where applicable
E24 English language proficiency certificate such as IELTS or TOEFL, where applicable
Financial-need evidence such as E09 recent payslip, E22 tuition arrears or fee balance statements and E23 university correspondence demonstrating financial hardship
selection_criteria: Only complete applications for eligible programmes, submitted before the deadline, in English and in accordance with the guidelines are considered; missing mandatory documents make an application incomplete and ineligible
Academic talent combined with financial disadvantage
Female applicants, persons with disabilities and applicants from other disadvantaged backgrounds are strongly encouraged; the Programme aims for at least 50% female participation
coverage: Full tuition fees payable directly to the host university
Monthly stipend of EUR 380 for accommodation, meals, local transport and other living expenses
Return economy-class air ticket between home and host country
EUR 200 arrival allowance; EUR 650 study materials allowance; one-time EUR 1,500 study and research allowance
Medical insurance for the duration of the scholarship; visa/entry fee where required; participation in at least one extracurricular event
application_method: Review the call and select a programme and university from the published list of 60 eligible Master's programmes
Apply for admission to that university, declaring the intention to apply for the EAC Scholarship Programme and paying any application fee
Complete the online EAC Scholarship Application form
Compile all mandatory supporting documents into a single folder named by the prescribed document codes, compress into a single zipped PDF folder

Email the folder to eacsp@iucea.org and scholarships@adroitconsultinternational.com using the subject line format '[Applicant Name] - Application for [Master's Programme] at [University] - Phase II EACSP'
official.application_route: Two-stage: Part A - apply for admission to a partner university; Part B - complete the online EAC Scholarship Application form and email the zipped PDF document pack to eacsp@iucea.org and scholarships@adroitconsultinternational.com with the prescribed subject line
official.citizenship_residency: Citizens of the 8 EAC Partner States: Burundi, Democratic Republic of Congo, Kenya, Rwanda, Somalia, South Sudan, United Republic of Tanzania and Uganda
official.international_eligibility: Restricted to EAC Partner State nationals; study must be at a participating university in an EAC Partner State other than the country of citizenship
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Thematic areas: Mathematics, Engineering, Informatics, Science, Technology and Business Science; applicants must choose from the 60 listed eligible Master's programmes at participating universities
official.description: The EAC Scholarship Programme is a regional initiative of the East African Community and the Federal Republic of Germany, implemented by IUCEA, developing future leaders who contribute to regional integration and sustainable development by supporting Master's studies in an EAC Partner State other than the scholar's country of citizenship.
official.english_requirement: Applications must be submitted in English. Supporting documents in languages other than English must be submitted with both the original and an English translation by an accredited language translation provider. An English language proficiency certificate such as IELTS or TOEFL is an optional supporting document where applicable.

verification.notes: Package amounts (EUR 380 monthly stipend, arrival, study materials and research allowances), tuition arrangement, eligibility, document codes, two-stage process and the 20 August - 10 September 2026 cohort window read directly from the live IUCEA Cohort 4 call page on 2026-10-10.

applicant_utility.summary: The EAC Scholarship Programme funds a full two-year Master's in mathematics, engineering, informatics, science, technology or business science at a university in a neighbouring EAC country - tuition, a EUR 380 monthly stipend, flights, insurance and study allowances - for EAC nationals under 35 with a strong bachelor's degree and demonstrable financial need. The trap is the two-stage process: a university admission application is not a scholarship application, and you must also file the separate online EAC scholarship form and email a zipped PDF pack to both IUCEA and the programme administrator. Cohort 4 closed on 10 September 2026, so the practical move now is to assemble documents and watch IUCEA's call-for-applications page for the next Phase II cohort.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Financially disadvantaged EAC nationals under 35 with a Second Class Upper Division or Distinction bachelor's degree, targeting a listed Master's programme across a border in a neighbouring EAC country.
application_readiness_checklist: Pick one or more of the 60 listed programmes and map each to its university's own admission process and fee
Start the university admission application early - it is a separate, parallel process that Part B depends on
Get non-English transcripts and certificates translated by an accredited provider, keeping originals and copies
Ensure foreign qualifications are equated by the host country's higher-education council or competent authority before admission
Prepare the document pack named by the E01-E24 codes as a single zipped PDF and rehearse the exact email subject-line format
common_rejection_risks: Treating the university admission application as the scholarship application - the separate online form is mandatory
Missing a mandatory document from the E01-E08 core set, which makes the file incomplete and ineligible
Applying to a programme not on the eligible list, or to a university in your own country of citizenship
Missing financial-need evidence (payslips, fee-balance or hardship letters) where applicable, weakening the disadvantage case
Age 35 or over at the time of application
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The package covers tuition, the EUR 380 monthly stipend, flights, insurance, arrival, study materials and research allowances and visa/entry fees; dependants' costs, anything beyond the stipend and expenses outside the published allowances are self-funded.
document_audit: E01 national ID or passport is mandatory - without it the file is automatically incomplete
Files must be named by document code (e.g. 'E04') inside a single zipped PDF folder
Degree certificate and transcript copies must be certified true copies
The email must go to both eacsp@iucea.org and scholarships@adroitconsultinternational.com with the prescribed subject line
Each additional programme application needs its own form, email and complete document set
alerts: Cohort 4 closed 10 September 2026 at 17:00 EAT; Phase II covers three cohorts from October 2025, so monitor IUCEA's call-for-applications page for the next window
Awards cannot be deferred or transferred - failing to take up the award at the time offered terminates it
At least 50% female participation is a programme aim; women, persons with disabilities and disadvantaged applicants are explicitly encouraged
Only shortlisted applicants are contacted, and false, misleading or incomplete information can trigger disqualification or withdrawal even after award
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Twofold process: first apply for admission to a partner university (Part A), then complete the online scholarship form and email the zipped document pack to both IUCEA and the administrator addresses with the prescribed subject line (Part B); successful students and host universities are informed in December.
